short_definition: A security system requiring two or more independent credentials to verify a user identity.
layman_explanation: Requiring both a keycard (something you have) and a PIN code (something you know) to enter a building.

short_definition: Granting users only the minimum access level necessary to perform their assigned work tasks.
layman_explanation: Giving a contractor a keycard that opens only the room they are renovating, not the entire corporate headquarters.

short_definition: An authentication scheme enabling a user to log in once and access multiple related applications.
layman_explanation: A master wristband at an amusement park that lets you enter every ride without purchasing separate tickets.

short_definition: Assigning permissions to predefined job roles rather than individual human user accounts.
layman_explanation: Issuing 'Manager Keycards' to all store managers instead of making custom badges for each employee name.

short_definition: An open delegation protocol enabling applications to gain limited access to user accounts on another service.
layman_explanation: Giving a valet key to a parking attendant that unlocks the ignition but keeps the glovebox locked.

short_definition: Specialized control systems designed to secure, monitor, and audit administrative accounts.
layman_explanation: A high-security vault holding master keys that records who took a key, when, and for what exact job.

short_definition: An automated cyberattack using stolen username-password pairs across thousands of different websites.
layman_explanation: Taking a stolen set of house keys and trying them on every front door across the entire neighborhood.

short_definition: A security model assuming no user or device is trusted by default, requiring continuous verification.
layman_explanation: Checking ID badges at every hallway door inside a building, rather than just at the front main entrance.

short_definition: Linking a user identity across multiple distinct security domains and different organizations.
layman_explanation: Using your government passport to verify your identity when entering private locations abroad.

short_definition: An authorization model evaluating rules based on user attributes, environment, and resource properties.
layman_explanation: Allowing entry only if you are an employee (user), during business hours (environment), wearing safety boots (attribute).

short_definition: A passwordless login standard utilizing cryptographic key pairs backed by biometric device unlock features.
layman_explanation: Unlocking your online accounts using your smartphone fingerprint or FaceID rather than typing text passwords.

short_definition: Stealing an active authenticated session cookie to gain unauthorized user access.
layman_explanation: Stealing a visitor hand-stamp at an event entrance so you can re-enter disguised as that person.

short_definition: Verifying identity through unique human biological characteristics such as fingerprints or iris scans.
layman_explanation: Unlocking a secure vault door using your unique facial geometry instead of a physical metal key.

short_definition: Granting elevated administrative rights temporarily for exact durations necessary to complete a task.
layman_explanation: Giving a maintenance worker a digital pass that automatically expires after 30 minutes.

short_definition: A fraud attempt where attackers illegitimately gain control of a genuine user's account credentials.
layman_explanation: Stealing someone's wallet and using their credit cards before the owner notices and cancels them.
